name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the following first-order linear ODE for the function $y=y(x):$

$$
{x}^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}+xy={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,x>0
$$

Write the equation in the form $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(yI(x))=I(x)Q(x),$ where $I(x)$ is an integrating factor.

Question 4
?

Consider the following first-order linear ODE for the function y=y(x): x2dydx+xy=x2cos⁡x,x>0 Write the equation in the form ddx(yI(x))=I(x)Q(x), where I(x) is an integrating factor.

a
ddx(yx2)=x2cos⁡x
b
ddx(yln⁡x)=ln⁡xcos⁡x
c
ddx(yx)=xcos⁡x
d
ddx(ye−x)=e−xcos⁡x
e
ddx(yex)=excos⁡x
